narrative.overview:
The Board is read the way a commuter reads a Seoul subway sign: no column labels, just a coloured line, a bold station name and the line under it that says where it goes. Every Product rides its own fixed line colour, every Incident's title is set like a station name with its CVE ID under it, the CVSS score is a ring whose arc runs to its value, and the reader understands a row in one glance. Risk sits apart from the lines as a square-cornered badge (a pale wash with dark same-hue text) at the row start, and the product lines are round pills, so "which line" and "how dangerous" never share a colour or a shape.

Density is that of a departure board: rows of 72 px minimum, one hairline between them, generous column gaps, nothing decorative in the rows. The ground is graphite at night and pale concourse paper by day; the visitor's system setting picks one and a remembered toggle overrides it. The "주요 사건" group stands apart as one alert band: a thin frame, a hairline between Highlights, each opening on a header strip (risk sign, 공격 발생 and its evidence, time) the way a disaster text opens on its header (critique P2, 11-19).

The Normal view is restrained: calm type, quiet colour, the facts. The Easy view is the same board with a friendlier voice: the risk word gains its "!", the row leads with a plain headline ("SonicWall VPN 인증 우회 위험 발견") over one plain sentence in Sign Ink, and each opened row ends in one plain action line set heavier than the text around it. The sign does not change; only the announcement does.
keyCharacteristics: No column header row; the row's grid position carries the meaning.
Two separate colour alphabets: risk and severity (red, amber, slate) and Product lines (eight fixed hues).
The Incident title as the bold name over its CVE ID, like a station name over its direction (owner, 11-09).
CVSS as a ring whose arc runs to the score out of 10, number inside; the ring itself is never filled.
Flat rows on hairlines; the Highlights band is framed, never lifted, washed or edged in colour.
Light and dark twins from one set of `light-dark()` tokens.

rules.name: The Two Alphabets Rule
rules.body: Risk and severity speak only in red, amber and slate (Clear Green is a third, separate alphabet for "done", never for risk), and the same severity is always the same colour; Product lines never use a red, orange, amber or grey hue, and a line colour never signals risk. Adding a line colour means checking it against all three first. Amber has two uses outside a risk level, both owner's (11-19): the warning banners (stale data, a failed load) and a filter chip that would leave nothing (dashed, on `caution-wash` in `caution-ink`).

rules.name: The Fixed Line Rule
rules.body: A Product's line colour is a function of its Product id, never its translated name, the same on every row and every visit. Never pick a line colour per page or per row.

rules.name: The Station Name Rule
rules.body: In the normal view the Incident title in the page language is the bold name and the CVE ID sits under it in Description size (owner, 11-09: "Headline first"); with more CVEs the line adds "외 N건". The Easy view leads with the Summary's plain headline over its one plain sentence (Sign Ink, 500, never cut); without a Summary the quick title leads, and an Incident with no CVE yet says so on the line under it. On 주의 rows a headline ending in "위험" ends in "문제" instead ("risk" → "issue"), so only 경계 and 긴급! rows speak of danger; the page swaps the word by the rule-based level, the Summary is unchanged.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: CVE IDs, counts, dates and times use tabular numerals so columns of numbers do not shimmer.

rules.name: The No Header Row Rule
rules.body: The Board never shows a row of column labels. If a column needs a label to be understood, the column is wrong.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: No row, band, field, button or opened detail casts a shadow (the raised segment above aside). The phone filter sheet and the floating filter panel are set apart by the Scrim (`--scrim`, 45% black over the Board), not by a lift.

dos: Do open every source link in a new tab (`target=_blank`, `noopener noreferrer`, a hidden "새 탭에서 열림" for screen readers), so the Board, its filters and opened rows stay put.

Do let a long line badge name wrap inside its pill wherever every name is listed (the opened row, the suggestions); only a closed row's badge keeps one line and ends in "…", its tooltip giving the whole name (11-19).
Do list several 해당 조건 one per line; never join them with " · " (a condition may hold its own dot, "팩스·SMS").
Do draw the focus ring inside a 주요 사건 row (`outline-offset: -3px`): the band clips anything outside it.

Do use the `:root` tokens (`--tap`, `--ctl-h`, `--ctl-fill`, `--ctl-hover`, `--ctl-on`, `--seg-on`, `--r-marker`, `--r-code`, `--r-ctl`, `--r-frame`, `--r-pill`, `--fs-meta`, `--fs-small`, `--skel`, `--warn-wash`, the lifts `--lift-low`, `--lift-menu` and `--lift-float`, the curves `--ease-out` and `--ease-exit`), the shared `.btn` for any new button (`.primary` only for the one main action in view) and the shared `.menu` / `.mi` for any new dropdown. A few colours stay literal on purpose: the CVSS ring's day and night tones and the new-Incidents pill's inverted blue (`web/index.html`), and the Support badge's yellow.
Do say "새 탭에서 열림" to screen readers on every link that opens a new tab, the Board's own buttons included (GitHub, 틀린 내용 알리기, Buy Me a Coffee).
Do keep every interactive target at least 44 px under a finger. Under a mouse controls are drawn 36 px (`--ctl-h`, Astryx, 11-19) and a folded source line 24px; layout heights keep `--tap`.
Do theme browser surfaces from the palette: selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring, link underline offset (3px).
Do keep Normal view calm and let the Easy view carry the louder voice (levels 긴급! / 경계 / 주의, "!" only at 긴급, a plain headline, one plain sentence that may end in "!", one action line at 17px/800).
Do check both themes for WCAG 2.2 AA contrast after any colour change.
Do write a device or Product badge with its vendor in front.
donts: Don't add a column header row to the Board.
Don't give a Product line a red, amber or grey hue, or use a line colour for risk.
Don't put shadows on rows, the Highlights band, fields or buttons (a segmented control's raised segment aside).
Don't give any row a coloured side edge; risk is said by the sign, a group by its tag (and an open fold's rail).
Don't set a column of numbers without tabular numerals.
